title: GPT-5.6 Sol
content: OpenAI’s flagship GPT-5.6 reasoning model and a key reference point for high-capability coding, research and agent work.

title: GPT-5.6 Terra
content: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 tier positioned between flagship and lighter variants, illustrating the shift toward task-based model routing.

title: GPT-5.6 Luna
content: OpenAI’s lighter GPT-5.6 option for everyday work, making capability, latency and cost trade-offs visible to normal users.

title: Claude Fable 5.1
content: Anthropic’s September 2026 model focused on fast, capable everyday work and agentic workflows.

title: Claude Mythos 5.1
content: Anthropic’s September 2026 high-end model for demanding reasoning and agentic work.

title: Claude Sonnet 5
content: Anthropic’s balanced Claude 5 family member, relevant to coding, enterprise work and agents.

title: Gemini 3.8 Flash
content: Google’s September 2026 fast Gemini model aimed at reasoning, coding and agentic tasks with strong latency economics.

title: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber
content: A security-focused Gemini 3.8 variant aimed at cyber reasoning and defensive workflows.

title: Grok 4.6
content: xAI’s 2026 model update emphasizing long-running agents, interactive work and visual capabilities.

title: DeepSeek V4 Pro
content: DeepSeek’s production-focused V4 model with major agent upgrades, adjustable reasoning effort and Responses API support.

title: DeepSeek V4 Flash
content: DeepSeek’s lower-latency V4 model optimized for agentic coding and Responses API workflows.

title: DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision
content: DeepSeek’s experimental multimodal V4 Flash variant for visual understanding inside agent workflows.

title: Llama 4 Scout
content: Meta’s open-weight multimodal Llama model designed for efficient deployment and very long context.

title: Llama 4 Maverick
content: Meta’s larger Llama 4 multimodal mixture-of-experts model for stronger general reasoning and vision tasks.

title: Mistral Medium 3.5
content: Mistral’s frontier-class multimodal model optimized for agentic and coding use cases.

title: Mistral Small 4
content: Mistral’s efficient open model combining instruct, reasoning and coding behavior in one model.

title: Qwen
content: Alibaba’s major model family spanning language, coding and multimodal workloads across a broad open ecosystem.

title: Cohere
content: Enterprise-focused AI platform known for retrieval, embeddings and business deployment patterns.

title: Perplexity
content: AI-native answer and research product that helped make citation-backed search a mainstream AI interface.

title: Hugging Face
content: The central distribution and collaboration layer for much of the open-model ecosystem: models, datasets, demos and libraries.

title: OpenAI
content: Frontier AI lab and platform behind ChatGPT, GPT-5.6 and Codex; a core reference point for consumer and developer AI.

title: Anthropic
content: Frontier AI company behind Claude, with strong emphasis on enterprise agents, coding, reliability and safety.

title: Google DeepMind
content: Google’s frontier research and model organization behind Gemini and much of the company’s advanced AI research.

title: xAI / SpaceXAI
content: The xAI ecosystem around Grok and large-scale compute, increasingly focused on agentic and multimodal systems.

title: Meta AI
content: Meta’s consumer and developer AI layer spanning assistants, open models, coding and generative media.

title: Microsoft Copilot
content: Microsoft’s AI layer across work apps, Windows and business workflows, increasingly agentic rather than just chat-based.

title: GitHub Copilot
content: AI coding platform evolving from autocomplete into multi-step coding agents and software-development workflows.

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
content: AWS infrastructure for building and operating production agents with identity, observability, governance and runtime controls.

title: Apple Intelligence / Siri AI
content: Apple’s privacy-oriented AI stack, with Siri AI adding personal context, screen awareness and deeper cross-device assistance.

title: Codex
content: OpenAI’s coding-agent surface for delegating software tasks across local, cloud and repository workflows.

title: Agentic AI
content: AI systems that pursue goals through multiple steps, tools and state rather than answering one prompt at a time.

title: Long-running agents
content: Agents that operate for minutes or hours across many tool calls, requiring durable state, monitoring, recovery and cost controls.

title: Coding agents
content: Software agents that inspect repositories, edit code, run tests and increasingly own complete development tasks.

title: Computer use
content: Models operating graphical interfaces through clicks, typing and visual understanding when APIs are unavailable.

title: Tool use
content: The ability for a model to call external tools, APIs, browsers, databases and code environments as part of a task.

title: Function calling
content: Structured model-to-software invocation that turns natural-language intent into typed application actions.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
content: A common protocol for exposing tools and context to AI applications, reducing one-off integration work.

title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A)
content: Patterns and protocols for specialized agents to discover, delegate and exchange work with one another.

title: Agent orchestration
content: The routing, sequencing, state, permissions and recovery layer that coordinates multiple models and tools.

title: Multi-agent systems
content: Architectures where specialized agents collaborate, debate or divide work instead of relying on one general agent.

title: Context engineering
content: Designing the information, tools, memory and constraints supplied to a model so it performs reliably over longer workflows.

title: Context windows
content: The amount of text, code, images or other tokens a model can consider at once; large windows reshape research and codebase workflows.

title: AI memory
content: Persistent user, project or task state that lets assistants continue work without rebuilding context every session.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
content: Grounding model responses in retrieved documents or data instead of relying only on model parameters.

title: Embeddings
content: Vector representations used for semantic similarity, retrieval, clustering and recommendation.

title: Vector databases
content: Stores optimized for similarity search over embeddings, commonly used as one component of retrieval systems.

title: Semantic search
content: Search based on meaning rather than exact keywords, now a standard building block for AI-native knowledge systems.

title: Structured outputs
content: Schema-constrained model responses that make LLMs safer and easier to connect to software systems.

title: Prompt caching
content: Reusing repeated context computation to reduce latency and inference cost in long or repetitive workflows.

title: Model routing
content: Choosing the best model per task based on quality, latency, safety and cost instead of sending everything to one frontier model.

title: Reasoning models
content: Models optimized to spend more computation on difficult problems before producing an answer.

title: Reasoning effort
content: A controllable setting that trades latency and cost for deeper inference on harder tasks.

title: Inference-time scaling
content: Increasing compute during inference rather than only during training to improve difficult reasoning performance.

title: Test-time compute
content: Extra sampling, search, verification or deliberation performed while solving a task; central to modern reasoning systems.

title: Evals
content: Repeatable tests that measure whether a model or agent actually performs the tasks a product depends on.

title: Benchmarks
content: Standardized comparisons for reasoning, coding, science and multimodal capabilities; useful but easy to overfit.

title: Agent benchmarks
content: Evaluations focused on multi-step tool use, coding, browsing and task completion rather than single-turn answers.

title: Guardrails
content: Policy and runtime controls that constrain unsafe or unwanted behavior around models and agents.

title: AI observability
content: Tracing prompts, tool calls, costs, latency, errors and outcomes so agent systems can be debugged and governed.

title: Human-in-the-loop
content: Workflow design where people review or approve high-impact steps instead of granting agents unlimited autonomy.

title: Multimodal AI
content: Models that work across text, images, audio and video in one system rather than treating each medium separately.

title: Vision-language models
content: Models that jointly understand images and language, powering visual search, document work and computer-use agents.

title: Speech-to-speech
content: Conversational AI that listens and responds directly in audio for lower-latency voice interaction.

title: Speech-to-text (STT)
content: Transcription that turns live or recorded audio into text for assistants, search, meetings and voice interfaces.

title: Text-to-speech (TTS)
content: Synthetic speech used for assistants, narration, accessibility and automated media production.

title: Image generation
content: Text- and image-conditioned visual generation, now a normal component of creative and product workflows.

title: Video generation
content: Generative models that create or transform moving images, rapidly moving from demos into production media pipelines.

title: LTX-2.5
content: LTX Studio’s current video model in its creator stack, relevant for scalable image-to-video and production workflows.

title: Audio-to-video
content: Generating or driving video from an audio track, useful for automated explainers, podcasts and character-led content.

title: Agentic video understanding
content: Video models that inspect long footage, reason over events and support tools or agents instead of merely captioning clips.

title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin
content: NVIDIA’s next-generation AI platform aimed at the agent era, emphasizing much lower inference cost and higher-scale systems.

title: NVIDIA Blackwell
content: The GPU platform underpinning a large share of frontier training and inference deployments before Rubin ramps fully.

title: AI factories
content: Data-center systems designed as continuous token-production infrastructure rather than conventional general-purpose compute.

title: GPU clusters
content: Large interconnected accelerator fleets used to train frontier models and serve high-throughput inference.

title: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)
content: Memory technology critical to feeding modern accelerators fast enough for large-model training and inference.

title: Inference economics
content: The cost per useful token or completed task; increasingly as important as raw benchmark quality when choosing models.

title: Mixture of Experts (MoE)
content: Architecture that activates only subsets of model parameters per token to scale capability more efficiently.

title: Quantization
content: Reducing numerical precision so models use less memory and compute, enabling cheaper cloud or local inference.

title: Distillation
content: Training smaller models to reproduce useful behavior from larger teachers, trading some capability for lower cost and latency.

title: Edge AI
content: Running models on phones, PCs, cars and devices for privacy, latency and offline capability rather than always using the cloud.

title: Synthetic data
content: Machine-generated training or evaluation data used to expand coverage, improve reasoning and reduce reliance on scarce labeled examples.

title: Post-training
content: The stage after pretraining where models are tuned for reasoning, instruction following, tool use, safety and product behavior.

title: Fine-tuning
content: Adapting a base model to a domain, task or style using additional examples or preference data.

title: Reinforcement learning
content: Training through rewards or environment feedback, increasingly important for reasoning, agents and tool-use behavior.

title: RLHF / RLAIF
content: Preference-learning methods using human or AI feedback to shape model behavior after pretraining.

title: Open weights
content: Models whose parameters can be downloaded and run independently, enabling customization, local deployment and sovereign AI.

title: AI safety & alignment
content: Research and engineering aimed at keeping increasingly capable systems reliable, controllable and consistent with intended goals.

title: Red teaming
content: Adversarial testing used to uncover failure modes, misuse paths and dangerous capability before deployment.

title: Model cards
content: Documentation that summarizes a model’s intended use, evaluations, limitations and safety characteristics.

title: Content provenance & watermarking
content: Techniques for signaling where digital media came from and whether it was generated or transformed by AI.

title: Sam Altman
content: OpenAI CEO and one of the most visible figures shaping the commercial frontier-model and AGI conversation.

title: Dario Amodei
content: Anthropic CEO and a central voice on frontier capability, scaling, safety and the economic impact of advanced AI.

title: Demis Hassabis
content: Google DeepMind CEO, connecting frontier model development with long-horizon scientific and AGI research.

title: Jensen Huang
content: NVIDIA CEO and a key architect of the accelerated-computing infrastructure powering the AI boom.

title: Elon Musk
content: Founder of xAI and a major force behind Grok, large-scale compute investment and the public debate around advanced AI.

title: Mark Zuckerberg
content: Meta CEO and the highest-profile major-tech advocate for a broad open-model ecosystem.

title: Satya Nadella
content: Microsoft CEO overseeing the company’s shift toward Copilot, agents and AI-native enterprise software.

title: EU AI Act
content: Europe’s risk-based AI regulatory framework, increasingly relevant to product design, compliance and deployment decisions.

title: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)
content: The contested idea of AI matching or exceeding human general cognitive capability across a very broad range of tasks.

title: Superintelligence
content: AI capability substantially beyond humans across most domains; increasingly discussed as a concrete governance and strategy horizon.
